title: navigator agent
goal:
need to create an agent that is working with ambicode context, it accepts a free text prompt, on the first step adapts this prompt with collected knowledge about repo (separate file/folder only for this, not the whole context folder) picking keywords that actually helps to spot features it mentions. then reads those files on a structure level, spots deps out of selected boundaries and checks what is imported. 
then filter the list to keep the only task related files and their deps and returns the result. if it gets any new info that could help to adapt the prompt better, it adds/refactors that file

phases.title: Baseline and design are fixed: a subagent reads the on-hold navigator plan (`/Users/KillBill/.claude/plans/current-src-is-overcomplicated-polymorphic-spindle.md`) and the current scout/context code, then reports in one page where the agent lives (skill, agent file, or route step), where the keyword file lives (its own file/folder under `.ambicode/`, separate from `context/`), its format, and how many files today's map (~2) and the earlier navigator (~52) return on the bench cases; decisions go to DECISIONS.md and the user approves the design before any code

Feature map file exists and is seeded from the repo: `.ambicode/navigator/` holds a feature map where each entry is a feature name, its domain terms and aliases (e.g. 'user management, migration, location modal'), its files, and its deps (services, models), within a stated size budget; a seed is built from the repo itself (file stems and declared names, no new ecosystem tables); unit tests on a fixture (`node fixtures/materialize.mjs`) show the file is created, stable across two runs and under budget

Navigator agent returns a task file list on the bench fixture: one fixture repo is chosen for all navigator runs (the local NDA nav repo with the most cases that have truth lists, materialized once and persisted, so features.md carries over from run to run); `agents/navigator.md` takes a free-text prompt, reads the feature map to adapt it into keywords, uses a CLI structure command (exports/imports/signatures via existing harvest) on matches, follows deps one hop out of the selected files, and returns only task files plus their deps; the CLI part has unit tests and the seed is measured on that fixture (size, time); one paid agent run on one case of it (after approval) is scored for recall/precision against truth

Navigator eval is a tracked suite: the bench run (navigator and bare arms, cases in date order on the one persistent bench repo) is registered in the repo's eval tracking the way other suites are (history, per-case scores, cost, the app's eval runner if it can carry a persistent repo), with NDA data kept outside the repo and referenced by env/path; verified by unit tests and a $0 dry run that writes one tracked record from the existing run-2 artifacts

Learning updates the feature map on the bench fixture: after a run the agent proposes entries learned while collecting files and code merges them into the persisted features.md (dedupe terms, drop paths no longer in git, cap 30 entries / 2500 tokens); unit tests cover the merge; on the same fixture a prompt that does not name its feature misses or partly misses on its first run and the later related run finds it from the updated map, with nothing outside `.ambicode/navigator/` edited

Eval compares the agent with bare on the one fixture: the fixture's cases run in a fixed time order with features.md persisting between runs, each run graded for recall and precision of the returned file list against truth; the bare arm runs the same cases on a fresh copy without the map; learning lift = later-run recall vs. first-run recall and vs. bare; no route integration; after the user approves, one paid sequence per arm (x3 if the user agrees), results logged with plan_log

Results are recorded and the branch is green: `npm run verify` passes (layering and guard bundle size included), STATE.md, DECISIONS.md and the plugin version are updated, and route integration plus harvest's ecosystem patterns are listed as deferred items with the measured numbers that would justify them

Generic-word cutoff halves cands but costs 1/3-1/2 coverage. Conclusion: map does not beat path search; scout map wiring (B) not justified as built.
